 Richard Riakporhe offers to fight Deontay Wilder on Fury-Joshua card
 by Scott Christ Nov 17, 2026, 6:09 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Getty Images for Netflix Scott Christ is the managing editor of Bad Left Hook and has been covering boxing for SB Nation since 2006. Richard Riakporhe has thrown a challenge into the wind, offering to step in and fight Deontay Wilder , who will no longer face Jai Opetaia on December 11.
 Opetaia has withdrawn from the bout . Dan Rafael has reported that Derek Chisora is a likely replacement, but Riakporhe has thrown his name into the ring.
 Wilder and Chisora fought earlier this year, with Wilder winning a brutal, 12-round decision.
 The 36-year-old Riakporhe (20-1, 16 KO) is 3-0 as a heavyweight since moving up from cruiserweight in 2025, and won the British title from Jeamie TKV by TKO-5 on April 11.
 Opetaia was also moving up from cruiserweight to face the 41-year-old Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KO) on the Fury vs Joshua undercard at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales.
 The card also has Martin Bakole slated to face Solomon Adebayo in a 10-round heavyweight fight, and in theory one of them could have switched to fighting Wilder, too, but that hasn’t been floated publicly. Bakole would make the more sense of the two.
 The biggest option, as much as it matters as it will be contributing roughly zero sold tickets to the card, would definitely be Chisora (36-14, 23 KO), whose supposed retirement following the loss to Wilder on April 4 has not been taken seriously by much of anyone, including by Chisora himself. At 42, he’s eons past his peak, but he always provides a brawling style that fans enjoy.
 It’s unlikely you could recapture the old man magic of the first Wilder-Chisora fight, especially on an undercard, but Wilder may also be more comfortable accepting a fight with a predictable veteran, and someone he’s already fought, than the more wild card nature of Riakporhe entering the fray.
